messages:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT HIGH — us-west-2a inference path error spike detected. 5xx rate > 30% for last 2m across gen and chat endpoints. Auto-page oncall. Priority: P1.

maria (oncall): got it. paging in. looking at dashboards now — traces show spike at NLB -> instance level.

dan (sre): I see connection resets from several hosts in us-west-2a. ENI transmit errors in host metrics, packet drops.

maria (oncall): is it widespread across all instances or a single ASG?

dan (sre): spread across 3 ASGs in the zone. per-host rx/tx errors followed by rsyslog kernel logs: "NETDEV WATCHDOG".

kevin (netops): this smells like NIC/driver or host-level offload degradation. AWS console showing increased ENI detach counts in us-west-2a for unrelated customers too. opening AWS support case now.

maria (oncall): impact note for customers: inference latency 500-2000ms, some 502s. CS, please prep a short blurb. @jamal

jamal (cs): prepping: "We’re seeing elevated errors for requests routed to us-west-2a; we’re routing traffic away where possible and working on mitigation. No data loss. We'll update in 30m." Will send to >10 affected tenants after we confirm routing change.

leah (eng-runtime): quick question — can we fall back to model-variants in other AZs without client-visible change? We have warm kvcache warmers in us-west-2b/c?

dan (sre): kvcache is region-wide but node-local warm cache lives per AZ. if we shift traffic to 2b/2c we’ll see initial small latency bump as caches repopulate. that's acceptable.

maria (oncall): action plan: 1) divert new traffic away from us-west-2a via control plane steering. 2) drain unhealthy hosts in 2a. 3) open AWS support (kevin) and get ETA. 4) notify customers. Assigning tasks: kevin -> AWS, dan -> host drains + rolling replacement, leah -> validate cross-AZ fallback, jamal -> customer comms.

kevin (netops): AWS case opened: #1234567891 — reported RX/TX driver/kernel NIC errors in us-west-2a affecting ENI attachments. AWS acknowledged potential host-level NIC incidents, investigating hypervisor hosts.

maria (oncall): leah, can you trigger a routing rule now? We have the control-plane API to reweight by AZ. Example: curl -X POST "https://internal-control.redwood/v1/steer" -d '{"region":"us-west-2","avoid_az":"us-west-2a","weight_shift":"round_robin"}' (pseudo).

leah (eng-runtime): performing steer now. executing rollout in incremental steps (10% -> 50% -> 100%) to avoid thundering herd. posting commands and progress.

leah (eng-runtime): STEP 1: 10% diverted off 2a -> success. token routing shows 10% drop to 2b/2c, latency bump ~60ms for a subset only.

maria (oncall): monitoring error rate.

incidents-bot: METRIC UPDATE: 5xx rate dropped from 31% -> 18% after 10% divert (1m).

leah (eng-runtime): STEP 2: increased to 50% traffic steer. running health checks.

dan (sre): starting draining: marking 12 hosts as IN_SERVICE=false in ASG; will cordon and drain workloads, then terminate to get fresh hosts.

kevin (netops): AWS update: they see elevated ENI detaches tied to a subset of hardware. mitigation ETA unclear, recommended customers steer traffic.

incidents-bot: METRIC UPDATE: 5xx rate now 7% after 50% divert. p95 latency improved.

jamal (cs): sending customer message now — short and to the point. cc'ing priority customers.

maria (oncall): continuing to 100% divert. leah, proceed when ready.

leah (eng-runtime): setting final 100% steer off us-west-2a. starting 40s ramp.

incidents-bot: REROUTE COMPLETE: traffic to us-west-2a is now 0% for inference routes. System reports stable.

maria (oncall): dan — keep draining until ASGs show zero active inference tasks; ensure no model loads retry storms. use --graceful-timeout 300s.

dan (sre): running drain command: 
```
for i in $(cat hosts_to_drain); do ssh root@$i 'systemctl stop inference-agent && sleep 10 && kubectl drain node/$i --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300'; done
```
I'll watch queue depth.

kevin (netops): AWS case updated: they flagged an underlying NIC firmware issue and will schedule host remediation. their recommended action is customer-side traffic steering (what we did). keeping case open.

maria (oncall): good. next: escalate to infra lead if AWS ETA > 2h.

jamal (cs): customers ack'ing. one enterprise customer asked for an availability timeline — I gave verbal ETA "under investigation; steering done; we'll notify when AWS provides remediation ETA."

leah (eng-runtime): post-steer checks: - KV cache miss rate spike transient 20% -> normalized in 3m - model load queue increased by 1.2x during steer; observed small error retries but no user-visible failures after steer.

incidents-bot: LOG: auto-run playbook 'single-az-fallback' completed with manual signoff.

maria (oncall): handoff plan: current oncall to keep monitoring for 30m. after that, handoff to night SRE (sre-night) for long-tail observation and additional node replacements. leave AWS case open.

sre-night: taking handoff at +30m. I'll watch for recurrence and coordinate with infra tomorrow for host replacements. please add any remaining steps.

maria (oncall): closing incident channel once AWS gives host remediation ETA. final notes: steering successful, customers notified, drains in progress, AWS case active #1234567891. Incident severity will be downgraded to P2 once error rate stays <1% for 15m.

jamal (cs): will follow up on customer threads and send a post-incident summary once we have host remediation details.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated, mitigation=traffic_steer_off_az, case=1234567891, owner=maria (oncall).
